_about: One entry per calculator page. Fields are rendered into the form by scripts/build_site.py; the math lives in assets/calc-core.js (single source of truth, also used for the worked examples). Units: 'length' ft|m, 'small' in|cm, 'area' ft2|m2, 'coverage' ft2/gal|m2/L, 'density' t/yd3|t/m3. Energy calculators are U.S.-only.

calculators.title: Electric Bill Calculator by State (Official EIA Rates)
calculators.short: Estimate a monthly bill from your usage and your state's current rate.
calculators.description: Estimate your monthly and yearly electric bill from your kWh usage and your state's latest average residential rate from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
calculators.intro: Pick your state to load its latest average residential price, then enter the kWh from your bill. Add your utility's fixed monthly charge if you know it.

fields.label: Monthly usage
fields.help: Your bill shows this as kWh used. The default is your state's average home.

fields.label: Price per kWh
fields.help: Loads your state's latest average. Replace it with the rate on your bill if you have it.

fields.label: Fixed monthly charge
fields.help: Many utilities add a customer charge, often around $10 to $25 a month.

how: Energy cost = monthly kWh × price per kWh. The bill estimate adds your fixed monthly charge on top.

State prices are averages of everything residential customers paid divided by the kWh they used, so they already include typical delivery charges, riders and fees. Your own rate can be higher or lower, especially on tiered or time-of-use plans.
tips: Divide your bill's total by its kWh to get your own all-in price, then compare it with your state's average.
If your usage is far above your state's average in a mild month, look for one big load: an old water heater, a pool pump or electric resistance heat.

faqs.q: How do I find my monthly kWh?
faqs.a: It is printed on every bill, usually next to the meter readings as 'kWh used' or 'usage'. Many utilities also show the last 12 months as a chart.

faqs.q: Why is my real bill higher than the estimate?
faqs.a: State averages smooth out tiers, time-of-use pricing and local taxes. Enter the per-kWh rate from your own bill and your fixed charge for a closer number.

calculators.title: Appliance Energy Cost Calculator: Cost per Hour, Day and Month
calculators.short: What an AC, space heater or dryer costs to run per hour and per month.
calculators.description: Find out how much any appliance costs to run per hour, day, month and year at your state's latest electricity price.
calculators.intro: Choose an appliance or type its wattage from the label, then set how long it runs. The price loads from your state's latest average.

fields.label: Power draw
fields.help: Typical running watts. Check the label or manual for your model.

how: kWh = watts ÷ 1,000 × hours. Cost = kWh × price per kWh.
Thermostat-controlled appliances (air conditioners, heaters, fridges) cycle on and off, so real use is often lower than the label wattage times the hours they are switched on.
tips: A plug-in energy meter shows the real kWh a device uses over a week, which beats any estimate.
Heating and cooling are usually the biggest lines on a bill, so they are where savings show up first.

faqs.q: How much does a 1,500 W space heater cost per hour?
faqs.a: It uses 1.5 kWh per hour, so multiply 1.5 by your price per kWh. At 18¢ that is 27¢ an hour.

faqs.q: Where do I find an appliance's wattage?
faqs.a: On the rating label or nameplate (often on the back or inside the door) and in the manual. If only amps are listed, watts ≈ amps × volts.

calculators.title: EV Charging Cost Calculator by State: Cost per Mile vs Gas
calculators.short: Home charging cost per month and per 100 miles, compared with a gas car.
calculators.description: Estimate what it costs to charge an electric car at home in your state, per month and per 100 miles, and compare it with a gas car.
calculators.intro: Enter how far you drive and your car's efficiency. The electricity price loads from your state's latest average; type your local gas price to compare.

fields.label: EV efficiency
fields.help: Most EVs travel roughly 3 to 4 miles per kWh. Check your car's rating.

fields.label: Charging losses
fields.help: Energy lost between the outlet and the battery, often around 10%.

fields.label: Your gas price
fields.help: Type the price at your local station.

how: kWh from the outlet = miles ÷ miles per kWh ÷ (1 − charging losses). Charging cost = kWh × electricity price.
Gas cost = miles ÷ mpg × gas price. The difference is what you would save (or spend) by charging at home instead of buying gas.
tips: Public fast charging usually costs several times more per kWh than home charging.
Some utilities offer cheaper overnight EV rates; ask yours and enter that price.

faqs.q: How many kWh does it take to drive 100 miles?
faqs.a: At 3.5 miles per kWh, about 28.6 kWh reaches the battery, or about 31.7 kWh from the outlet with 10% charging losses.

faqs.q: Is charging at home always cheaper than gas?
faqs.a: At typical U.S. home electricity prices it usually is, but in states with very high rates and for very efficient gas cars the gap narrows. The calculator shows your own numbers.

calculators.title: Solar Payback Calculator 2026 by State (No Federal Credit)
calculators.short: Years to pay back a rooftop system, using NLR PVWatts output for your state.
calculators.description: Estimate rooftop solar payback and 25-year savings using your state's PVWatts production estimate and latest electricity price, updated for 2026 without the expired federal credit.
calculators.intro: Production per kW loads from the NLR PVWatts model for a large city in your state. Enter the price from your installer's quote for a real answer.

fields.label: Installed price per watt
fields.help: From your quote: total price ÷ system watts. Quotes vary widely by state and installer.

fields.label: Rebates and incentives
fields.help: State or utility rebates only. The 30% federal credit for homeowner-owned systems (Section 25D) ended on December 31, 2025.

fields.label: Yearly output per kW
fields.help: Loads the NLR PVWatts estimate for your state. Your installer's estimate for your roof is better.

fields.label: Value of each solar kWh
fields.help: 100% if every kWh offsets a full retail kWh. Lower it if your utility credits exports at a lower rate.

how: System cost = size × 1,000 × price per watt − rebates. Year-one output = size × yearly output per kW.

Each year's savings = output × electricity price × value of each solar kWh. Prices rise by the yearly increase you set and output falls by the panel loss. Payback is the first year when total savings reach the system cost.
tips: Get at least three quotes and compare them by price per watt, not by monthly payment.
If your utility pays less for exported power, a battery or shifting use to daytime raises the value of each kWh.

faqs.q: Is the 30% federal solar tax credit still available in 2026?
faqs.a: Not for systems you buy. The residential clean energy credit (Section 25D) ended on December 31, 2025. Companies that lease systems or sell power under a PPA can still claim a business credit, which may lower those offers.

faqs.q: Where does the production estimate come from?
faqs.a: From PVWatts, the solar model run by the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), for a fixed roof-mounted system facing south at a 20° tilt with 14% system losses.

calculators.title: Concrete Calculator: Cubic Yards and Bags for a Slab
calculators.short: Cubic yards and 40, 60 or 80 lb bags for a slab, patio or footing.
calculators.description: Work out how much concrete you need for a slab in cubic yards or cubic meters, and how many 40, 60 or 80 lb bags of premix to buy.
calculators.intro: Enter the slab's length, width and thickness. Add a little extra for uneven ground and spillage.

fields.label: Thickness
fields.help: Patios and walkways are usually 4 in (10 cm) thick; driveways often 5 to 6 in.

how: Volume = length × width × thickness, plus the extra percentage. One cubic yard is 27 cubic feet.
Premixed bags yield about 0.60 ft³ (80 lb), 0.45 ft³ (60 lb) and 0.30 ft³ (40 lb). Check the bag, because yields vary by brand.
tips: Above roughly one cubic yard, ready-mix delivery is often cheaper and faster than mixing bags.
Measure thickness in several spots; a 4 in slab that ends up 4.5 in thick needs 12.5% more concrete.

faqs.q: How many 80 lb bags make a cubic yard?
faqs.a: About 45. A cubic yard is 27 ft³ and each 80 lb bag yields about 0.60 ft³.

faqs.q: How much concrete for a 10 × 10 slab, 4 inches thick?
faqs.a: 33.3 ft³, or 1.23 cubic yards, before extra. With 10% extra that is about 1.36 yd³ or 62 bags of 80 lb.

calculators.title: Gravel, Mulch and Topsoil Calculator: Cubic Yards and Tons
calculators.short: Cubic yards, tons and bags for gravel, sand, topsoil or mulch.
calculators.description: Calculate how many cubic yards or cubic meters of gravel, sand, topsoil or mulch you need, with an estimate in tons and in 2 ft³ bags.
calculators.intro: Choose the material, then enter the area and depth you want to cover.

fields.label: Depth
fields.help: Mulch beds: 2 to 3 in. Gravel paths: 3 to 4 in.

fields.label: Weight per volume
fields.help: Typical dry values. Wet material weighs more; ask your supplier.

how: Volume = length × width × depth, plus the extra percentage. One cubic yard is 27 cubic feet.
Weight = volume × weight per cubic yard. Typical figures: about 1.4 tons per yd³ for gravel, 1.35 for sand and 1.1 for topsoil.
tips: Bulk delivery is priced per cubic yard or per ton; bags make sense for small beds.
Lay landscape fabric under gravel paths so the stone doesn't sink into the soil.

faqs.q: How many bags of mulch are in a cubic yard?
faqs.a: 13.5 bags of 2 ft³, because a cubic yard is 27 ft³.

faqs.q: How much does a cubic yard of gravel weigh?
faqs.a: Usually around 1.4 tons (about 2,800 lb), depending on the stone size and how wet it is.

calculators.title: Paint Calculator: How Many Gallons for a Room
calculators.short: Gallons or liters for a room's walls and ceiling, minus doors and windows.
calculators.description: Estimate how much paint you need for a room's walls and ceiling, in gallons or liters, after subtracting doors and windows.
calculators.intro: Enter the room's size and how many doors and windows it has. Most paints cover 350 to 400 square feet per gallon per coat.

fields.label: Coverage
fields.help: From the can's label, per coat.

how: Wall area = 2 × (length + width) × height. Doors and windows are subtracted, and the ceiling (length × width) is added if you tick it.
Paint needed = area × coats ÷ coverage per gallon (or liter).
tips: Buy whole gallons for the main color and keep a little for touch-ups.
A primer coat helps when you cover a dark color or bare drywall.

faqs.q: How much paint for a 12 × 12 room?
faqs.a: With 8 ft walls, one door and two windows, about 334 ft² of wall. Two coats at 350 ft² per gallon need about 1.9 gallons, so buy 2.

faqs.q: Do I really need two coats?
faqs.a: Usually yes for an even color, especially when changing colors. Some one-coat paints cover well over a similar shade.

calculators.title: Drywall Calculator: Sheets and Screws for a Room
calculators.short: How many 4×8, 4×10 or 4×12 sheets a room needs, plus screws.
calculators.description: Calculate how many drywall sheets you need for a room's walls and ceiling, with an allowance for waste and an estimate of screws.
calculators.intro: Enter the room's size and pick a sheet size. Openings are not subtracted, because the offcuts rarely get reused.
how: Area = 2 × (length + width) × height, plus length × width for the ceiling. Sheets = area with extra ÷ sheet area, rounded up.
Screws: about one per square foot of board, which is about 32 for a 4 × 8 sheet.
tips: Longer sheets mean fewer joints to tape and finish.
Use moisture-resistant board in bathrooms and laundry rooms.

faqs.q: How many sheets of drywall for a 12 × 12 room?
faqs.a: With 8 ft walls and the ceiling, 528 ft². With 10% extra that is about 581 ft², or 19 sheets of 4 × 8.

faqs.q: Should I subtract doors and windows?
faqs.a: For small openings, no. The pieces you cut out are usually waste, so counting the full wall keeps you from running short.

calculators.title: Flooring and Tile Calculator: Square Feet and Boxes
calculators.short: Square footage plus waste, and how many boxes to buy.
calculators.description: Work out the floor area of a room, add the right allowance for waste, and see how many boxes of tile, laminate or vinyl plank to buy.
calculators.intro: Enter the room's size and the coverage printed on one box. Use 10% extra for a straight layout and 15% for diagonal or herringbone.

fields.label: Coverage per box
fields.help: Printed on the box or product page.

how: Floor area = length × width. Material needed = area × (1 + extra %). Boxes = material needed ÷ coverage per box, rounded up.
tips: Buy all boxes from the same batch or dye lot so the color matches.
Keep one spare box for future repairs.

faqs.q: How much extra flooring should I buy?
faqs.a: About 10% for straight layouts in simple rooms, and 15% or more for diagonal or herringbone patterns and rooms with many corners.

faqs.q: How many boxes for a 12 × 10 room?
faqs.a: 120 ft² plus 10% is 132 ft². With 20 ft² boxes, that is 7 boxes.

calculators.title: Roofing Calculator: Roof Area, Squares and Shingle Bundles
calculators.short: Roof area from the footprint and pitch, in squares and shingle bundles.
calculators.description: Estimate roof area from your house footprint and roof pitch, and see how many squares and bundles of shingles you need.
calculators.intro: Measure the footprint including the overhangs, then enter the pitch as inches of rise per 12 inches of run.
how: Pitch factor = √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²). Roof area = footprint × pitch factor, plus the extra percentage.
A roofing square is 100 ft². Most asphalt shingles come in 3 bundles per square; some heavier styles need more, so check the wrapper.
tips: Hips, valleys and dormers add cutting waste; use 12 to 15% extra on complex roofs.
Order ridge cap and starter strip separately; they are not included in the bundle count.

faqs.q: What is a roofing square?
faqs.a: 100 square feet of roof surface.

faqs.q: How many bundles for a 40 × 30 roof at 6/12?
faqs.a: 1,200 ft² × 1.118 = 1,342 ft² of roof. With 10% extra that is 14.8 squares, or 45 bundles at 3 per square.
